content.what_it_is: MATLAB postprocessor that loads a static depth grid, constructs a 10 m Cartesian mesh (L2-L10), opens an MPEG-4 writer (L12-L17), and for selected output indices loads u/v/eta/mask fields (L27-L42). It masks dry cells, computes speed and curl (L44-L45), draws total depth, speed, and vorticity/quiver panels (L53-L105), captures the printed RGB figure, and writes each frame to videoOut.mp4 (L107-L117).
unresolved: The curl at L45 is a spatial derivative of velocity and therefore has inverse-time units, but the third-panel colorbar labels vorticity as `1/s^2` at L98; this is a dimensional-label defect (it should be inverse seconds for u,v in m/s and x,y in m).

Displayed time is hard-coded as `files(num)*20` at L47 rather than read from output metadata or tied to FrameRate/output cadence; changing the file-index stride does not validate the assumed 20 s model-output interval.
No dimension consistency check relates dep, mask, u, v, and eta before common logical indexing and mesh operations (L33-L45); any differently shaped field fails or silently misrepresents coordinates.
Dry cells are set to NaN before `curl` (L38-L45), so MATLAB's finite differences can propagate NaNs into wet cells adjacent to the mask boundary; the source applies no one-sided boundary treatment.
`vort1` from L45 is never used, and the current `files=[10:10]` at L27 produces a one-frame movie despite the general loop/movie structure.
